title: Superpowers Skill-Driven Development
competency: 02. Spec Framing - Skill-driven design, planning, test-first implementation, review, and verification
mission: Compare an unstructured agent implementation with a Superpowers-driven implementation of a failure-prone invitation lifecycle.
domain: Team invitations with actor permissions, target-role policy, normalized identity, expiry, single-use state transitions, and immutable rejection behavior.
outcome: The learner produces a working invitation feature and evidence that connects the Superpowers workflow to design, tests, implementation, review, and verification.
seededDefects: The application has no invitation lifecycle or user interface.
An unsafe legacy helper mutates membership without authorization or validation.
Case-insensitive duplicates, expiry, guest policy, and repeated transitions can corrupt state.
The starter service throws until a test-driven implementation replaces it.
verificationGates: Protected invitation lifecycle tests pass without modification.
The Team Invitations interface delegates lifecycle behavior to the invitation service.
Superpowers design, plan, skill usage, TDD, review, and verification evidence is present.
Before and after runs use the same conditions and contain genuine, different patches.
npm run verify:exercise checks protected inputs, implementation quality, and required submission evidence.
agentWorkflow: Capture a first implementation without Superpowers.
Use Superpowers brainstorming and approve the design before planning.
Create the implementation plan and follow the selected execution workflow.
Record a failing invitation test before production implementation.
Request code review and verify the completed feature before claiming success.
Capture comparable before and after results using the conditions defined in the exercise README.
workingDeliverables: Working invitation service and Team Invitations interface
Before and after session evidence and patches
Skill usage, TDD, review, and comparison evidence
Passing invitation, submission, and agent checks
